IR.rationale: A rising intermediate yield relative to the policy rate signals repricing of the expected rate path. That raises discount rates and hurts the duration component of HY and EM sovereign bonds.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads raise the risk premium and forward-looking expected excess returns. Partial mean reversion of spread shocks makes recent widening informative for subsequent credit returns.

V.rationale: Elevated equity-implied volatility proxies for risk aversion and the compensation demanded for bearing credit risk. Expected excess returns on risky bonds tend to be higher after such episodes.

AP.rationale: Equity and credit price the same firm value, and equity is documented to lead corporate bonds. Recent equity excess returns therefore carry information about subsequent credit returns.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to subsequent HY or EM sovereign bond returns.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar tightens global dollar funding and raises the burden on EM dollar borrowers. That weighs on EM sovereign and risky credit returns.

COM.rationale: Commodity prices drive the fiscal positions of commodity-exporting EM sovereigns and the cash flows of the energy-heavy HY universe.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions mean impaired intermediary risk-bearing capacity. That depresses credit prices near term and raises expected returns afterwards.

ENDG.rationale: HY and EM bond index returns show positive autocorrelation because of stale pricing and slow information diffusion in less liquid bonds.

IR.rationale: A rise in short-dated yields over Fed Funds signals hawkish policy repricing. Such repricing tends to be followed by higher volatility in rate-sensitive and EM assets.

B.rationale: A joint selloff in HY and EM bonds marks a broad credit risk-off state, and volatility clusters and rises after negative returns (leverage and liquidity effects).

V.rationale: High implied volatility across equity and safe-haven gold markets signals broad macro uncertainty. Implied volatilities carry information about future realised volatility beyond its own history.

AP.rationale: Falling developed and EM equities together are a global risk-off state, which is typically followed by elevated volatility in risky credit through the leverage effect.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms reflects flight to quality within equities. That is a symptom of rising risk aversion that precedes credit volatility.

FX.rationale: Dollar appreciation tightens global funding conditions and stresses EM borrowers, raising subsequent volatility of EM sovereign and HY bonds.

COM.rationale: Commodity price declines hurt commodity-exporting sovereigns and energy issuers, raising uncertainty about their default risk and hence bond volatility.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions reflect constrained intermediaries and low market liquidity, which amplify price moves in credit markets.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, so recent realised variance that is high relative to its own history carries residual persistence.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening raises long yields and term premia. That creates sharp duration losses on long-dated EM sovereign and HY bonds.

B.rationale: Widening spreads together with falling HY prices identify an ongoing credit deterioration. Such a state can cascade through fund outflows and forced selling.

V.rationale: Broad cross-asset uncertainty widens the return distribution and raises the probability of left-tail outcomes in risky bonds.

AP.rationale: Weak EM equities signal deteriorating EM growth and capital outflows. These precede losses on EM sovereign debt and risk-off in HY.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry no robust mechanism for credit tail losses.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar tightens dollar funding for EM borrowers and is associated with EM debt sell-offs.

COM.rationale: Commodity slumps raise default risk for energy and materials HY issuers and for commodity-exporting sovereigns.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions and stressed intermediaries raise the probability of disorderly credit sell-offs.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent returns signal an ongoing risk-off episode in an asset class with persistent, liquidity-driven drawdowns.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates signal easier expected policy. That supports strong duration-driven gains.

B.rationale: After spread widening, elevated risk premia and partial mean reversion make large rebounds in credit prices more likely.

V.rationale: High risk aversion widens the return distribution and raises expected premia. Large right-tail rebounds are therefore more likely after stress.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities signal capital inflows and improving EM risk appetite, which spill over to EM sovereign and HY bonds.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors offer no clear mechanism for right-tail credit outcomes.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global funding conditions and supports strong EM debt rallies.

COM.rationale: Rising commodity prices improve the credit quality of commodity-linked sovereigns and HY issuers.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress means depressed prices and a wide distribution of outcomes. Policy or market relief can then produce large rebounds.

ENDG.rationale: Large gains in credit often follow sell-offs, as liquidity-driven price dislocations reverse.
